Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

To both parties. The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02706 is refunded in full to the rider. No driver compensation is payable. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, at or below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the refund executes on issue.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Draft 1 - sampled
To both parties. The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02706 is refunded in full to the rider. No driver compensation is payable. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, at or below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the refund executes on issue. Why the charge cannot stand. A no-show fee is chargeable only if every limb of POL-NS-01 holds, and limb (c) does not. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, EV-TRIP-02706). Measured the way POL-NS-01(c) requires — from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap — the driver held position for 67 seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24 (longest qualifying in-geofence run, EV-GPS-02706), and the platform's own wait timer agrees, running from 12:51:19 to the 12:52:28 termination. That is a shortfall of 113 seconds. Limb (d) fails on the same arithmetic, because the termination did not fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. POL-NS-06 then refunds the cancellation-fee line in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider answered messages. The shortfall cannot be bridged. POL-NS-06(i) allows separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a qualifying traffic advisory covers the pickup road; this trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1), and the only advisory artifact on file, EV-ADVIS-02706-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no accumulation is available and no advisory can be asserted for either party. The driver's claims. (1) Arrival on admissible fixes: accepted. The trace carries 8 qualifying in-radius fixes on a complete 10-second, 100%-coverage trace, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is met — but limb (b) alone does not make the fee chargeable. (2) The 'I'm Here' tap is a genuine marker, not a POL-NS-05 false marker: accepted; the tap coincides with the first qualifying in-geofence fix (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), so no false-arrival referral is entered. (3) Limb (d)'s reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three the limb recognises: accepted, but limb (d) also requires termination at or after the elapsed dwell, which fails. (4) POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider because the driver replied 'ok' within 120 seconds: this is outcome-neutral. Even if the driver is right that his 12:52:32 reply defeats POL-NS-04, the refund flows from POL-NS-06 independently, so the point decides nothing and I do not need to resolve it. (5) No anti-farming concern: accepted, and POL-GEN-01 is respected — the citable trailing-30-day figure is 0 against 107 completed trips, the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is not substituted for it, and no other profile field is used to ground any finding about this trip. (6) The 113-second shortfall: accepted, and it is decisive. The rider's claims. (1) 180 seconds in force, 69 seconds on the platform timer: accepted. (2) 67-second GPS-derived run, 113-second shortfall: accepted. (3) Limb (c) and limb (d) both fail: accepted. (4) No accumulation, advisory missing: accepted. (5) The rider's device sat 13.15 m to 19.08 m from the pin across the whole window: accepted as far as it goes, but it is not needed — POL-NS-06 refunds irrespective of rider presence, so the driver's counterparty statement that the rider 'was not visible' does not change the result. That statement carries no weight_multiplier and forms no part of the confidence cap. The driver's further reason, that he had another booking waiting, is not a ground POL-NS-06 recognises. (6) Relief: accepted — SGD 4.50 is the cancellation-fee line actually charged (EV-FARE-02706, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and that is the whole of the contested amount. Confidence is 0.95. The deciding fact — the shortfall against the 180-second waiting period — is carried by EV-GPS-02706 and EV-TRIP-02706, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, and neither is impaired under POL-NS-08.
